approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It also retains stable canonical-identity admission and a direct, formula-preserving exchange of aromatic nitrogen positions. Each fresh surplus pool is evaluated by a binary-fingerprint Gaussian process trained on all accepted scores, and correlated posterior draws choose the oracle submissions. Accepted offspring can then enter the breeding population. The posterior currently uses the same small observation-noise level at every fit, even when its prediction errors differ substantially across the molecular neighborhoods encountered.
approach.novelty: Learn that single observation-noise level from the current accepted archive by comparing exact Gaussian marginal likelihoods over a fixed five-level menu. Larger selected noise represents mismatch between fingerprint similarity and accepted scores, reducing how tightly the posterior must interpolate them. Earlier posterior siblings changed binary environment presence into occurrence counts; this experiment retains the Parent's binary representation and instead tests whether task-local noise learning changes conditional uncertainty and improves prospective predictions. The graph, population and correlated-draw selection mechanisms remain inherited.

hypothesis: Choose the fingerprint Gaussian process's standardized observation-noise standard deviation at each fit by minimum exact negative log marginal likelihood over five fixed multiples of the inherited noise level, using only the current accepted archive.

finding_summary.headline: Noise learning changed 255 fits and improved matched coverage, but mean score fell 0.017540
finding_summary.insights:
Archive likelihood can identify and propagate substantial surrogate mismatch without improving the search endpoint. The matched measurements show better average coverage and predictive loss, but wider intervals still cover fewer than the nominal 95% of observed scores, and ranking gets weaker. Better uncertainty accounting is therefore insufficient evidence that the unchanged posterior-draw selector allocates evaluations more productively. The unchanged decoration and median trajectories also show that a measurable posterior change need not alter an emitted choice.

The remaining uncertainty problem includes score scaling. In an early sitagliptin batch, even the maximum standardized noise is multiplied by an archive scale of 0.001: a predicted mean of 0.00111 and total SD of 0.00118 precede a score of 0.18595, more than 157 SDs away. This narrows the next modeling question toward anticipating score-unit changes from a nearly flat accepted archive; expanding the menu alone is not established as a remedy. Frequent upper-endpoint selection leaves the appropriate noise range unresolved, while unchanged binary-fingerprint ties leave representational limitations intact.

The chemistry assessment also finds the existing structural liabilities intact, including unusually large repeated scaffolds, reactive heteroatom bonds, undefined stereochemistry and a new sulfur-radical branch. These observations limit what improved statistical coverage or occasional high scores mean chemically; they do not identify the cause of the aggregate score loss. The evidence establishes noise-learning activation and a failed score-benefit expectation on this panel, without isolating the causal value of any individual changed selection.
finding_summary.results:
The learned noise reached the actual posterior in 255 of 435 fits; 180 retained the reference level and 116 selected the largest allowed value. All five likelihood trials, final conditioning, accepted-label provenance and recorded posterior draws reconstructed correctly. After feedback, mean uncertainty on the admitted molecules remained 0.02821 score units, compared with 0.00405 under the fixed-noise rule on those same current archives.

On the 4,350 molecules actually submitted, the matched fixed-noise comparison shows latent 1.96-SD coverage rising from 79.68% to 82.44%. Including fitted observation noise raises observed-score coverage from 79.72% to 89.84%, with average interval width increasing from 0.1901 to 0.2604. Mean predictive negative log density improves from 6.3965 to 1.9102, and prediction MSE falls from 0.012180 to 0.011625 against an archive-mean baseline of 0.024654. Within-batch rank association weakens from 0.4146 to 0.3943. These are comparisons on identical accepted data and actual emissions.

Search utility declines: mean final-best score falls from 0.551771 to 0.534231, a paired loss of 0.017540 that misses the registered +0.002 benefit criterion. One seed improves and two decline; population standard deviation rises from 0.008223 to 0.023491. DRD2 and zaleplon task means fall, sitagliptin rises, and decoration and median retain exactly the same trajectories in every seed. Actual best-parent beats are essentially unchanged at 592 versus 593. All tasks and pools complete, with no numerical fallback; the additional 2,175 noise-trial factorizations consume 3.745 seconds of recorded unsynchronized host search time.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families with size extremes, labile heteroatom bonds, sulfur radicals and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Read all 15 Child and 15 Parent trajectory files, covering seeds 0, 1 and 2 on every supplied task; no task lacks trajectories. Each Child task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. All 4,350 Child proposal records parse with the supplied RDKit 2023.09.6; this establishes graph readability, not synthesis or stability. The digest's molecule-level string indicators give ring-closure rates of 0.9609 to 0.9908 and aromatic-token rates of 0.9460 to 0.9874. These indicate the presence of those features in SMILES, not aromatic atom fractions. The output is dominated by indole/pyrazole amides and thiocarbonyls, repeated heteroaromatic carbonyl units, halogenated aryl/polyamine systems, and fused or bridged ureides. Saturated rings and three-dimensional connectivity are present; their stereochemistry is unspecified. Passive graph counts find unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,274 proposals, with no assigned centres and no explicitly charged proposals. They also identify 73 radical-containing proposals, all in one sulfur-rich seed, 874 proposals with N-halogen bonds, 381 with O-halogen bonds and 163 with O-O bonds; these categories overlap and flag structures for chemical review, not measured reactivity. Graph variation is substantial, but high-score neighborhoods repeatedly elaborate a few functional-group families. Overall drug-likeness is weak because familiar medicinal fragments coexist with excessive molecular size, difficult ring connectivity and unusual electronic or functional-group states. Parent comparison is molecular and descriptive: the complete ordered evaluation/source/SMILES/score records are identical on deco_hop and median_2 for every seed. The other tasks change their molecular neighborhoods; none of these observations judges mechanism activation. All sizes, ring counts and structural flags below are passive descriptors of recorded molecules. Score readings are associations within the supplied trajectories; they do not reveal an absent reference structure or establish a binding mode, pKa, synthetic route or measured stability. Reproducible provenance and descriptor calculations are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-11-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have a median of 25 heavy atoms. Seed 0 concentrates on phenol-substituted pyrazoles with thiocarbonyl/thiourea linkages and unsaturated small carbocycles; seeds 1 and 2 favor alkyl/alkoxy indoles bearing aryl or pyridyl carboxamides. The seed-2 leader at evaluation 298 has 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings, an indole NH, ethoxy and methyl groups, a fluoropyridyl group and an N-fluoroamide. Seed 1 reaches an ordinary secondary-amide analogue, whereas the seed-0 leader has four rings, two aromatic, and a hydroxylated cyclobutene substituent. These are recognizable medium-sized heteroaromatic molecules, but the N-fluoroamide and strained/unsaturated ring substitutions make the panel only conditionally plausible as synthetic chemistry. Compared with the Parent, seed 0 shifts from a fused indole-related endpoint into the pyrazole/thiocarbonyl family; seeds 1 and 2 retain the indole/azaaryl-carbonyl neighborhood. Recorded best scores by seed change from 0.442313/0.460926/0.451975 to 0.420196/0.416350/0.438799, with similar molecular scale.
liabilities: The highest observed molecule contains an N-F bond in an amide; a late low-scoring structure combines N-F and O-F bonds with a thiocarbonyl. These are chemically sensitive connectivities, even though the SMILES sanitize.

Cyclobutene/cyclopentadiene substitutions and additional fused closures introduce strain or reactivity concerns; they cannot be treated as routine synthetic analogues solely because they retain the parent functional groups.
missing_features: The upper end does not demonstrate broad alternative ring/linker arrangements that preserve the favorable compact heteroaromatic and polar-group pattern beyond the recurring indole and pyrazole families. A specific absent target motif cannot be inferred from these scores.
Stereodefined forms of the newly substituted nonaromatic rings are not represented; this is a coverage gap, with no score evidence that a particular configuration would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.305105; the compact substituted indole and pyrazole endpoints reach 0.416350 to 0.438799. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 28 and 25, respectively, so retaining a compact heteroaromatic core matters more here than indiscriminate enlargement. The seed-2 evaluation-298 leader scores 0.438799, whereas evaluation 295, which has methoxy and aminomethyl substitutions, scores 0.304901. These are multiple simultaneous differences, not an isolated amine penalty. A Br/F substitution pair in the seed-1 leaders ties at 0.416350, while the elaborate thione/O-fluoro terminal proposal scores 0.091681. Very small proposals such as the cited halogen and hydrocarbon fragments score zero. The observed preference is for a particular compact arrangement of aromatic rings and polar carbonyl/thiocarbonyl groups, with substantial tolerance for chemically unusual substitutions; it does not establish that those unusual bonds cause the gain.

per_task.generated_character: This panel grows large, mostly aromatic assemblies: the proposal median is 69 heavy atoms and nine perceived rings. Seed 0 builds extended azaaryl/aryl carbonyl and ether assemblies; seed 1 repeats aryl and nitrogen/oxygen heteroaromatic carbonyl units with alkoxy, imine, nitrile/cyanate and chloromethyl-ether substituents. The seed-1 evaluation-295 leader has 91 heavy atoms, nine aromatic rings and calculated molecular weight about 1,303.5; evaluation 296 has 113 heavy atoms and 13 aromatic rings. Seed 2 is smaller, with a proposal median of 39 heavy atoms, but commonly joins two fused ureide systems through an amino-heteroaryl unit and introduces N-F, N-Cl or O-Cl bonds. The large repeated products are far outside ordinary small-molecule scale and would require substantial synthetic justification; even the smaller seed-2 series contains unusual reactive functionality. All ordered molecular records and scores match the Parent in all seeds.
liabilities: Very high molecular size, many linked aromatic rings and numerous acceptors create substantial solubility, conformational and synthesis concerns. These are structural concerns, not measured exposure or permeability results.

Chloromethyl ethers, imine/enol-ether segments and the smaller series' N-F/N-Cl/O-Cl bonds require stability and synthetic scrutiny; high scores do not establish that these are isolable, useful compounds.
missing_features: Compact, nonrepeated scaffolds retaining the heteroaromatic/carbonyl/aryl-ether arrangement seen at the upper end are not demonstrated at comparable scores. The missing coverage concerns economical placement of these features, not a shortage of rings or aromatic atoms.

The trajectories do not identify which unseen decoration or reference feature is absent; they show repeated functional-group assemblies rather than evidence for a particular target-specific replacement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The tiny cited fragments all sit at 0.5. Initial indole and fused ureide-containing molecules already score 0.546402 and 0.548381; elaborated aromatic assemblies reach 0.611413. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 38 and 85 and median aromatic-ring counts of four and ten. This is an association between the sampled favorable motifs and extensive aromatic elaboration, not evidence that adding arbitrary mass helps. The 91-heavy-atom leader scores 0.611413 and the 113-heavy-atom analogue scores 0.611206, showing that greater size is not monotonically rewarded. Seed 0 reaches 0.609808, seed 1 0.611413 and seed 2 0.597688. The cited compact seed-2 terminal analogue scores 0.577517, while the linked/fused larger terminal structures score around 0.588 to 0.597. High scalar scores therefore tolerate both repeated large architectures and N-/O-halogenated chemistry; no synthesis benefit follows from this gradient.

per_task.generated_character: The high end consists of medium-sized halogenated diaryl molecules with substantial saturated ring/linker content and several nitrogen centres. The proposal median is 36 heavy atoms; the high-score quartile is narrower, at 30 to 37 heavy atoms. Seed 2 builds amidine-containing, amino-substituted pyrrolidines connected through an NCN aminal segment to another aryl-bearing carbon. Its leading phenol has 31 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings plus a pyrrolidine, several potential protonation sites and three unassigned tetrahedral centres. Seed 0 instead retains small nitrogen rings attached to an aryl-substituted [SH](=N) sulfur centre; the supplied RDKit assigns one radical electron to that sulfur in the cited leaders. There are 73 radical-containing proposals in that seed, versus none in the Parent panel. Seed 1 favors polycyclic amine/sulfoxide structures. The Parent already produced compact diaryl/basic-nitrogen structures. Its recorded seed maxima of 0.979377/0.951235/0.991404 become 0.938121/0.829081/0.946088 here, alongside the new sulfur-radical branch and the amidine/polyamine branch.
liabilities: The [SH](=N) leaders carry a sulfur-centred radical by the matching RDKit's electron assignment. This is a stronger issue than merely uncommon sulfur nomenclature and is not detected by SMILES parse success alone.

Neutral SMILES for amidines/polyamines leave important solution-state charge possibilities unresolved. Multiple donors/basic sites, brominated aromatic groups and unspecified stereocentres complicate interpretation as a defined medicinal compound; no pKa, permeability or synthetic route is supplied.
Small strained nitrogen rings and NCN aminal connections warrant chemical stability and synthetic review even when the rest of the scaffold uses familiar fragments.
missing_features: Basic nitrogen centres are abundant. What is absent from the submitted representations is explicit protonation and defined stereochemistry for these existing centres and substituted saturated rings; downstream oracle protonation handling is not established by these trajectories.

The favorable compact diaryl/basic-group arrangement has not been broadly reproduced through simpler linkers and routinely closed-shell ring systems. The sulfur branch lacks a demonstrated closed-shell counterpart retaining its high-end arrangement, while the polyamine branch relies on an aminal and many polar/basic sites.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial large acidic sulfonamide scores 0.019041, and a truncated N-chloroamide/sulfonamide scores 0.000347. The leading diaryl/amidine/polyamine phenol scores 0.946088; replacing that phenol with an aniline gives 0.936709. Cited terminal molecules show that nitrogen abundance alone is insufficient: the analogue lacking the second aryl group scores 0.236533, an additional-amidine analogue scores 0.627986, and an enlarged three-aryl analogue scores 0.403056. These are not isolated edits, but together they favor a compact two-aryl/basic-nitrogen arrangement over extra size or indiscriminate polar-group addition. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 43 and 33. The two sulfur-radical leaders tie at 0.938121 despite changing one aryl Cl to F. This demonstrates that a high recorded docking objective can coexist with an electronically unusual submitted graph; it does not establish how the oracle treated that state or identify a receptor contact.

per_task.generated_character: These are mostly medium-sized, densely connected N/O heterocycles: the proposal median is 30 heavy atoms, five rings and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 develops constrained nitrogen-rich carbonyl systems attached to alkylated azaaryl groups; seed 1 favors phenyl/ethoxy-substituted fused or bridged ureide/enamine/ether architectures; seed 2 retains azaaryl-linked fused imide-like systems. The seed-1 evaluation-218 leader has 33 heavy atoms, five rings, two aromatic rings, cyclic carbonyl/urea functionality, an N-methyl group and an N,O-acetal carbon carrying an unassigned stereocentre. Its elemental functional groups are familiar, but its ring connectivity and medium-ring closures demand a specific synthetic route. This is genuine saturated and aromatic ring chemistry, not an aromatic-only string collection. All ordered molecular records and scores are identical to the Parent across all seeds.
liabilities: Dense annulation, medium-ring carbonyl systems and enamine/acetal connections make synthetic feasibility and conformational accessibility uncertain without a route or structural analysis.

Duplicating the heterocyclic framework adds size and rings while producing a lower-scoring cited terminal molecule; chemical complexity alone should not be read as meaningful new pharmacophore coverage.
missing_features: The upper end does not show a broad set of simpler alternative ring/linker topologies preserving the favorable aromatic/carbonyl/nitrogen arrangement; the recorded gain remains concentrated in densely fused or bridged ureide-related chemistry. The trajectory does not identify a particular absent reference scaffold.

Explicit configurations are missing where new ring junctions or N,O-acetal substitutions create tetrahedral centres. The missing information is stereochemical definition, not the capacity to generate saturated or three-dimensional graphs.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial fused ureide-containing molecule scores 0.167839. Later constrained carbonyl/amine systems reach seed maxima of 0.204784, 0.213610 and 0.207878. The seed-1 leaders at evaluations 218 and 203 score 0.213610 and 0.213010 with closely related 33-heavy-atom polycycles. The cited seed-2 terminal 28-heavy-atom, six-ring product scores 0.201130, while the larger duplicated 41-heavy-atom, eight-ring product scores 0.165558. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 32 and 31 and median aromatic-ring counts of three and two. The observed gradient favors particular compact, partly saturated arrangements of aromatic and carbonyl/nitrogen features, not simply more rings or larger molecules. Hydrocarbon and hydroxylamine fragments at the low end score zero or 0.012461. The terminal excerpt still varies substantially within the same functional-group families.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 27 heavy atoms. Seed 0 reaches compact fluorinated fused ureide-like heterocycles bearing several carbonyls, fluoroalkyl substituents, a fluorinated alkenyl chain and an N-SH substituent. The tied leaders have 28 heavy atoms, two aromatic rings and molecular weight about 426.4. Seed 1 favors fluorinated conjugated carbocyclic ketones attached to imino/carbonyl heterocycles with an N-F bond. Seed 2 instead develops more fused ring systems with peroxyester and N-halogen functionality. The seed-0 leaders therefore look more compact than many early aryl-rich products, but their N-SH chemistry is still unusual. The other seeds' N-F and peroxyester chemistry makes synthetic plausibility questionable. Relative to the Parent's compact fluorinated nitrogen/carbonyl systems, seed 0 changes toward the N-SH/fluoroalkyl ureide series and the other seeds toward different labile ring families. Recorded maxima change from 0.475978/0.575091/0.503080 to 0.663627/0.504586/0.411429.
liabilities: The leading n(S) substitution is an N-SH connection with a terminal sulfur hydrogen in the supplied RDKit, not an ordinary carbon thioether. Its persistence and synthetic handling are not established.

N-halogen bonds, conjugated unsaturated ketones and peroxyesters appear in the other seeds; these can be reactive motifs and require chemical review. The panel contains 79 peroxide-bearing proposals compared with five in the Parent, despite both panels having a median of 27 heavy atoms.
Large duplicated heterocycles and tiny fragments continue to appear late, so compact high-scoring chemistry is not maintained in every subsequent proposal.
missing_features: The high-end size and fluorinated/carbonyl balance is not demonstrated across a broad set of conventional stable functional-group arrangements: the best branch uses N-SH, while other upper-end branches contain N-F or peroxyester groups. The gap is reliable access to chemically ordinary alternatives, not missing fluorine, amides or rings.

Geometric specification of the unsaturated side chains and defined configurations in the more fused products are missing from the cited SMILES. No trajectory comparison establishes whether assigning those states changes the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-rich fused ureide ester scores 0.002094. A duplicated 60-heavy-atom, nine-ring ureide/aryl product scores 1.6758614448245604e-53, whereas the compact 28-heavy-atom leaders score 0.663627. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 31 and 27. Within the cited seed-0 series, lengthening one fluoromethyl substituent to fluoroethyl accompanies a change from 0.536196 to 0.663627. Moving which of the two nitrogen substituents carries that additional carbon leaves the two leaders tied at 0.663627. A related chloroethyl member scores 0.520929. These comparisons support sensitivity to the sampled size/composition and polar/fluorinated balance, without proving a unique required connectivity. Both extreme enlargement and the terminal acetylene fragment are poor: the latter scores 3.716764234274643e-25. A late seed-2 peroxyester-containing molecule scores 0.277703, while its enlarged peroxide-linked relative scores 1.5627949162950568e-19. The gradient clearly does not establish stability or justify peroxide chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Passive parsing finds 73 radical-containing optimizer proposals. The cited aryl/small-nitrogen-ring [SH](=N) leaders at score 0.938121 have one sulfur-centred radical electron in the matching RDKit. Every proposal still passes parsing, and the Parent trajectories contain no such radicals.
transferable_gaps.gap: The emitted structures do not consistently preserve closed-shell electronic states.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make electronic-state consistency explicit in generic molecular construction and admission, and support closed-shell alternatives to unusual sulfur connectivity. Parse success alone cannot serve as evidence of an ordinary stable molecular product; no objective identity is needed to address this gap.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across 4,350 proposal records, passive bond inspection finds N-halogen bonds in 874, O-halogen bonds in 381 and O-O bonds in 163. The cited high-scoring compact indole contains an N-fluoroamide; compact fluorinated ureides carry N-SH; later fused products carry peroxyesters. These are structural flags, not a measured instability count.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ordinary functional-group connectivity is not reliably retained during molecular variation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically informed ways to vary substituents and heteroatom placement while preserving recognizable functional groups, including stable alternatives to heteroatom-halogen, terminal N-SH and peroxide connections. Apply the same chemical rules and accepted-feedback learning to every objective, without treating an alert as proof that every occurrence is unusable.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited aromatic assemblies contain 91 and 113 heavy atoms with very similar scores, while a different cited duplicated 60-heavy-atom framework has a near-zero score. The complete proposal panel also contains 55 molecules with at most three heavy atoms. High-scoring neighborhoods elsewhere are compact ring-bearing molecules, so there is no universal larger-is-better rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecular scale is variable but insufficiently controlled against repeated-framework growth and collapse to tiny fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support local growth and contraction that retain useful ring/linker context and can remove duplicated substructures. Let already accepted score feedback determine where molecular elaboration matters, while preserving chemically meaningful intermediate sizes; the evidence does not justify one objective-specific size rule or a blanket ban on larger molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All digest stereocentre-marker rates are zero. Passive nonlegacy tetrahedral perception finds unassigned centres in 2,274 proposal records and assigned centres in none. The cited amino-substituted pyrrolidine leader has three unassigned centres, and the leading fused N,O-acetal has an unassigned centre as well.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator produces stereogenic graphs without producing explicitly defined stereoisomers.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and represent stereochemistry when edits create or modify stereogenic environments, and make alternative configurations available as chemically defined candidates under ordinary identity handling. This adds molecular-state coverage; the supplied scores do not establish which configurations would be favored.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task's digest charged-marker rate is zero and passive parsing finds no charged proposal. Nevertheless the cited leaders include amidines and multiple aliphatic amines, while supplied low and initial molecules include carboxylic acids. Neutral SMILES do not imply that those compounds stay neutral in solution.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit acid/base charge states are absent despite frequent potentially ionizable functional groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically consistent representations of ionizable centres and relevant protonation alternatives using a universal state policy. Preserve the distinction between the submitted representation and any downstream preparation; these trajectories alone neither reveal that preparation nor prove a score benefit from charge enumeration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The panel contains many distinct graphs, but the cited high-end families repeatedly elaborate fused ureides, indole/pyrazole carbonyl compounds or diaryl/basic-nitrogen systems. Some upper-end ureides have five interconnected rings and an N,O-acetal, while more elaborate duplicated terminal frameworks score below compact related examples. Rich ring counts therefore coexist with uncertain ring-closure feasibility.
transferable_gaps.gap: Dense ring rearrangements outpace evidence for simpler, synthetically interpretable alternative scaffolds.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand alternative ring and linker constructions that preserve useful functional-group arrangements with interpretable bond-forming relationships, rather than counting every added closure or duplicated framework as equivalent chemical coverage. Synthetic plausibility must be assessed as a property of the proposed structure, with no task name or hidden reference scaffold supplied.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

activation_observables.measurement: Reconstruct every trial covariance, exact negative log marginal likelihood including its actual jitter, deterministic minimum and final fitted noise from ordered previously accepted same-process identities and scores. Require no future, rejected, unselected-pool or cross-task label. Count selected SDs, reference-retaining fits, upper-endpoint selections and objective reductions by task and supplied seed. On the Child's identical archives and ordered pools compare its selected-noise posterior with the reference-noise Parent rule, holding features, kernel, normalization and numerical settings fixed. Report absolute changes in means, marginal SDs and full conditional covariance, with fixed-data changes above 1e-10 distinguished from numerical residue. Activation requires actual fits selecting SD above the reference and passing that selected noise into a measurably changed pool distribution. A logged selection unconnected to final conditioning does not activate the mechanism. Fits retaining the reference level are valid no-change cases; features and pre-noise kernel entries must remain exactly inherited.
activation_observables.name: Reconstruct each fit from its ordered accepted training records and declared feature/kernel/normalization/noise settings; report changed representations, similarity relationships or posterior values only on eligible fixed-data comparisons.

activation_observables.measurement: Join each nonterminal emitted molecule's prediction to its accepted score and the next fit's existing identical-molecule probe, recording both fitted noise levels and normalization scales. Compare before/after score-unit means and SDs, standardized conditional variances and a fixed-current-archive reference-noise probe. finding_summary.headline: Noise learning changed 255 fits and improved matched coverage, but mean score fell 0.017540
finding_summary.insights:
Archive likelihood can identify and propagate substantial surrogate mismatch without improving the search endpoint. The matched measurements show better average coverage and predictive loss, but wider intervals still cover fewer than the nominal 95% of observed scores, and ranking gets weaker. Better uncertainty accounting is therefore insufficient evidence that the unchanged posterior-draw selector allocates evaluations more productively. The unchanged decoration and median trajectories also show that a measurable posterior change need not alter an emitted choice.

The remaining uncertainty problem includes score scaling. In an early sitagliptin batch, even the maximum standardized noise is multiplied by an archive scale of 0.001: a predicted mean of 0.00111 and total SD of 0.00118 precede a score of 0.18595, more than 157 SDs away. This narrows the next modeling question toward anticipating score-unit changes from a nearly flat accepted archive; expanding the menu alone is not established as a remedy. Frequent upper-endpoint selection leaves the appropriate noise range unresolved, while unchanged binary-fingerprint ties leave representational limitations intact.

The chemistry assessment also finds the existing structural liabilities intact, including unusually large repeated scaffolds, reactive heteroatom bonds, undefined stereochemistry and a new sulfur-radical branch. These observations limit what improved statistical coverage or occasional high scores mean chemically; they do not identify the cause of the aggregate score loss. The evidence establishes noise-learning activation and a failed score-benefit expectation on this panel, without isolating the causal value of any individual changed selection.

Prospective uncertainty coverage increases in aggregate on the 4,350 actual Child emissions, with heterogeneous task/seed results. Every prediction is taken from an emission log line before the corresponding oracle score; both learned-noise and reference-noise calculations use exactly that same contemporaneous Child fit and actual emitted identity. No score is assigned to alternative indices or unselected pool molecules. Against this matched reference, learned-noise MSE decreases from 0.0121797120 to 0.0116253491; the same-fit archive-mean baseline is 0.0246544109. Mean within-batch average-rank correlation decreases from 0.414642 to 0.394342 across 435 defined batches. Latent interval coverage at one SD increases from 2,641/4,350 (60.7126%) to 2,673/4,350 (61.4483%); at 1.96 SD it increases from 3,466/4,350 (79.6782%) to 3,586/4,350 (82.4368%). Mean latent full widths [one SD,1.96 SD] increase from [0.0966604,0.189454] to [0.104730,0.205270]. Latent standardized residual mean/RMS change from -0.259317/4.22931 to -0.0246680/3.87701. Observed-score predictive variance is explicitly latent variance plus (fitted standardized noise SD times current score scale)^2; jitter is not added as measurement noise. Its coverage at one SD increases from 2,648/4,350 (60.8736%) to 2,965/4,350 (68.1609%), and at 1.96 SD from 3,468/4,350 (79.7241%) to 3,908/4,350 (89.8391%). Mean full widths [one SD,1.96 SD] rise from [0.0970086,0.190137] to [0.132851,0.260388]. Observed standardized residual mean/RMS change from -0.257773/4.21809 to -0.0285450/2.89380; mean Gaussian predictive negative log density decreases from 6.396454 to 1.910165. Wider intervals account for part of the coverage improvement; the lower predictive loss and modest MSE improvement are separately measured, and 1.96-SD coverage still falls short of a nominal 95% Gaussian interval. Coverage does not improve uniformly: DRD2 seeds 1 and 2 lose five and four latent-covered outcomes respectively versus the matched reference, despite larger latent variance. An informative remaining failure occurs in sitagliptin seed 1 batch 2: the selected maximum SD 0.8 is multiplied by a score scale of 0.001. A prospective mean 0.00110535 and total predictive SD 0.00117730 precede an accepted score 0.185949, a 157.006-SD residual. This single observation contributes 2.83211 to the panel mean predictive negative log density; it remains included in all metrics. It shows why standardized noise learning cannot alone anticipate large score-unit jumps while the accepted archive scale is tiny. Actual endpoint utility is separate: replica macro mean is 0.5342306436565504 versus Parent 0.5517706549878213, paired change -0.01754001133127092, below the registered +0.002 criterion. Population SD rises from 0.008223094871288588 to 0.023491242314783334. Paired seed macro changes are +0.024855414342, -0.047446933131 and -0.030028515205. Task mean changes are zaleplon -0.026622857220, decoration 0, DRD2 -0.069575036466, median 0 and sitagliptin +0.008497837030. There is one positive, eight negative and six equal task/seed endpoints. Decoration and median trajectories are byte-identical to the Parent for every seed, even though four decoration fits and one median fit change noise and the posterior. Actual Child proposals beat their best generating parent 592/4,350 times, versus Parent 593/4,350; actual incumbent improvements are 205 versus 217. Thus the score-benefit falsifier triggers while the implementation and aggregate coverage expectations are supported. The alternative reference-noise selector has no counterfactual scores, and downstream trajectory differences do not isolate individual uncertainty decisions. Complete per-task/seed prospective results follow. Each actual/reference pair uses the same 290 scored Child emissions; rank is the average of 29 within-batch correlations. Widths are full intervals, MSE is in squared score units, and density is in natural-log score units.

finding_summary.headline: Noise learning changed 255 fits and improved matched coverage, but mean score fell 0.017540
finding_summary.insights:
Archive likelihood can identify and propagate substantial surrogate mismatch without improving the search endpoint. The matched measurements show better average coverage and predictive loss, but wider intervals still cover fewer than the nominal 95% of observed scores, and ranking gets weaker. Better uncertainty accounting is therefore insufficient evidence that the unchanged posterior-draw selector allocates evaluations more productively. The unchanged decoration and median trajectories also show that a measurable posterior change need not alter an emitted choice.

The remaining uncertainty problem includes score scaling. In an early sitagliptin batch, even the maximum standardized noise is multiplied by an archive scale of 0.001: a predicted mean of 0.00111 and total SD of 0.00118 precede a score of 0.18595, more than 157 SDs away. This narrows the next modeling question toward anticipating score-unit changes from a nearly flat accepted archive; expanding the menu alone is not established as a remedy. Frequent upper-endpoint selection leaves the appropriate noise range unresolved, while unchanged binary-fingerprint ties leave representational limitations intact.

The chemistry assessment also finds the existing structural liabilities intact, including unusually large repeated scaffolds, reactive heteroatom bonds, undefined stereochemistry and a new sulfur-radical branch. These observations limit what improved statistical coverage or occasional high scores mean chemically; they do not identify the cause of the aggregate score loss. The evidence establishes noise-learning activation and a failed score-benefit expectation on this panel, without isolating the causal value of any individual changed selection.
finding_summary.results:
The learned noise reached the actual posterior in 255 of 435 fits; 180 retained the reference level and 116 selected the largest allowed value. All five likelihood trials, final conditioning, accepted-label provenance and recorded posterior draws reconstructed correctly. After feedback, mean uncertainty on the admitted molecules remained 0.02821 score units, compared with 0.00405 under the fixed-noise rule on those same current archives.

On the 4,350 molecules actually submitted, the matched fixed-noise comparison shows latent 1.96-SD coverage rising from 79.68% to 82.44%. Including fitted observation noise raises observed-score coverage from 79.72% to 89.84%, with average interval width increasing from 0.1901 to 0.2604. Mean predictive negative log density improves from 6.3965 to 1.9102, and prediction MSE falls from 0.012180 to 0.011625 against an archive-mean baseline of 0.024654. Within-batch rank association weakens from 0.4146 to 0.3943. These are comparisons on identical accepted data and actual emissions.

Search utility declines: mean final-best score falls from 0.551771 to 0.534231, a paired loss of 0.017540 that misses the registered +0.002 benefit criterion. One seed improves and two decline; population standard deviation rises from 0.008223 to 0.023491. DRD2 and zaleplon task means fall, sitagliptin rises, and decoration and median retain exactly the same trajectories in every seed. Prospective uncertainty coverage increases in aggregate on the 4,350 actual Child emissions, with heterogeneous task/seed results. Every prediction is taken from an emission log line before the corresponding oracle score; both learned-noise and reference-noise calculations use exactly that same contemporaneous Child fit and actual emitted identity. No score is assigned to alternative indices or unselected pool molecules. Against this matched reference, learned-noise MSE decreases from 0.0121797120 to 0.0116253491; the same-fit archive-mean baseline is 0.0246544109. Mean within-batch average-rank correlation decreases from 0.414642 to 0.394342 across 435 defined batches. Latent interval coverage at one SD increases from 2,641/4,350 (60.7126%) to 2,673/4,350 (61.4483%); at 1.96 SD it increases from 3,466/4,350 (79.6782%) to 3,586/4,350 (82.4368%). Mean latent full widths [one SD,1.96 SD] increase from [0.0966604,0.189454] to [0.104730,0.205270]. Latent standardized residual mean/RMS change from -0.259317/4.22931 to -0.0246680/3.87701. Observed-score predictive variance is explicitly latent variance plus (fitted standardized noise SD times current score scale)^2; jitter is not added as measurement noise. Its coverage at one SD increases from 2,648/4,350 (60.8736%) to 2,965/4,350 (68.1609%), and at 1.96 SD from 3,468/4,350 (79.7241%) to 3,908/4,350 (89.8391%). Mean full widths [one SD,1.96 SD] rise from [0.0970086,0.190137] to [0.132851,0.260388]. Observed standardized residual mean/RMS change from -0.257773/4.21809 to -0.0285450/2.89380; mean Gaussian predictive negative log density decreases from 6.396454 to 1.910165. Wider intervals account for part of the coverage improvement; the lower predictive loss and modest MSE improvement are separately measured, and 1.96-SD coverage still falls short of a nominal 95% Gaussian interval. Coverage does not improve uniformly: DRD2 seeds 1 and 2 lose five and four latent-covered outcomes respectively versus the matched reference, despite larger latent variance. An informative remaining failure occurs in sitagliptin seed 1 batch 2: the selected maximum SD 0.8 is multiplied by a score scale of 0.001. A prospective mean 0.00110535 and total predictive SD 0.00117730 precede an accepted score 0.185949, a 157.006-SD residual. This single observation contributes 2.83211 to the panel mean predictive negative log density; it remains included in all metrics. It shows why standardized noise learning cannot alone anticipate large score-unit jumps while the accepted archive scale is tiny. Actual endpoint utility is separate: replica macro mean is 0.5342306436565504 versus Parent 0.5517706549878213, paired change -0.01754001133127092, below the registered +0.002 criterion. Population SD rises from 0.008223094871288588 to 0.023491242314783334. Paired seed macro changes are +0.024855414342, -0.047446933131 and -0.030028515205. Task mean changes are zaleplon -0.026622857220, decoration 0, DRD2 -0.069575036466, median 0 and sitagliptin +0.008497837030. There is one positive, eight negative and six equal task/seed endpoints. Decoration and median trajectories are byte-identical to the Parent for every seed, even though four decoration fits and one median fit change noise and the posterior. Actual Child proposals beat their best generating parent 592/4,350 times, versus Parent 593/4,350; actual incumbent improvements are 205 versus 217. Thus the score-benefit falsifier triggers while the implementation and aggregate coverage expectations are supported. The alternative reference-noise selector has no counterfactual scores, and downstream trajectory differences do not isolate individual uncertainty decisions. Complete per-task/seed prospective results follow. Each actual/reference pair uses the same 290 scored Child emissions; rank is the average of 29 within-batch correlations. Widths are full intervals, MSE is in squared score units, and density is in natural-log score units.

finding_summary.headline: Noise learning changed 255 fits and improved matched coverage, but mean score fell 0.017540
finding_summary.insights:
Archive likelihood can identify and propagate substantial surrogate mismatch without improving the search endpoint. The matched measurements show better average coverage and predictive loss, but wider intervals still cover fewer than the nominal 95% of observed scores, and ranking gets weaker. Better uncertainty accounting is therefore insufficient evidence that the unchanged posterior-draw selector allocates evaluations more productively. The unchanged decoration and median trajectories also show that a measurable posterior change need not alter an emitted choice.

The remaining uncertainty problem includes score scaling. In an early sitagliptin batch, even the maximum standardized noise is multiplied by an archive scale of 0.001: a predicted mean of 0.00111 and total SD of 0.00118 precede a score of 0.18595, more than 157 SDs away. This narrows the next modeling question toward anticipating score-unit changes from a nearly flat accepted archive; expanding the menu alone is not established as a remedy. Frequent upper-endpoint selection leaves the appropriate noise range unresolved, while unchanged binary-fingerprint ties leave representational limitations intact.

The chemistry assessment also finds the existing structural liabilities intact, including unusually large repeated scaffolds, reactive heteroatom bonds, undefined stereochemistry and a new sulfur-radical branch. These observations limit what improved statistical coverage or occasional high scores mean chemically; they do not identify the cause of the aggregate score loss. The evidence establishes noise-learning activation and a failed score-benefit expectation on this panel, without isolating the causal value of any individual changed selection.
finding_summary.results:
The learned noise reached the actual posterior in 255 of 435 fits; 180 retained the reference level and 116 selected the largest allowed value. All five likelihood trials, final conditioning, accepted-label provenance and recorded posterior draws reconstructed correctly. After feedback, mean uncertainty on the admitted molecules remained 0.02821 score units, compared with 0.00405 under the fixed-noise rule on those same current archives.

On the 4,350 molecules actually submitted, the matched fixed-noise comparison shows latent 1.96-SD coverage rising from 79.68% to 82.44%. Including fitted observation noise raises observed-score coverage from 79.72% to 89.84%, with average interval width increasing from 0.1901 to 0.2604. Mean predictive negative log density improves from 6.3965 to 1.9102, and prediction MSE falls from 0.012180 to 0.011625 against an archive-mean baseline of 0.024654. Within-batch rank association weakens from 0.4146 to 0.3943. These are comparisons on identical accepted data and actual emissions.

Search utility declines: mean final-best score falls from 0.551771 to 0.534231, a paired loss of 0.017540 that misses the registered +0.002 benefit criterion. One seed improves and two decline; population standard deviation rises from 0.008223 to 0.023491. DRD2 and zaleplon task means fall, sitagliptin rises, and decoration and median retain exactly the same trajectories in every seed. Actual best-parent beats are essentially unchanged at 592 versus 593. All tasks and pools complete, with no numerical fallback; the additional 2,175 noise-trial factorizations consume 3.745 seconds of recorded unsynchronized host search time.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families with size extremes, labile heteroatom bonds, sulfur radicals and unresolved stereochemistry
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Read all 15 Child and 15 Parent trajectory files, covering seeds 0, 1 and 2 on every supplied task; no task lacks trajectories. Each Child task contains 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals. All 4,350 Child proposal records parse with the supplied RDKit 2023.09.6; this establishes graph readability, not synthesis or stability. The digest's molecule-level string indicators give ring-closure rates of 0.9609 to 0.9908 and aromatic-token rates of 0.9460 to 0.9874. These indicate the presence of those features in SMILES, not aromatic atom fractions. The output is dominated by indole/pyrazole amides and thiocarbonyls, repeated heteroaromatic carbonyl units, halogenated aryl/polyamine systems, and fused or bridged ureides. Saturated rings and three-dimensional connectivity are present; their stereochemistry is unspecified. Passive graph counts find unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2,274 proposals, with no assigned centres and no explicitly charged proposals. They also identify 73 radical-containing proposals, all in one sulfur-rich seed, 874 proposals with N-halogen bonds, 381 with O-halogen bonds and 163 with O-O bonds; these categories overlap and flag structures for chemical review, not measured reactivity. Graph variation is substantial, but high-score neighborhoods repeatedly elaborate a few functional-group families. Overall drug-likeness is weak because familiar medicinal fragments coexist with excessive molecular size, difficult ring connectivity and unusual electronic or functional-group states. Parent comparison is molecular and descriptive: the complete ordered evaluation/source/SMILES/score records are identical on deco_hop and median_2 for every seed. The other tasks change their molecular neighborhoods; none of these observations judges mechanism activation. All sizes, ring counts and structural flags below are passive descriptors of recorded molecules. Score readings are associations within the supplied trajectories; they do not reveal an absent reference structure or establish a binding mode, pKa, synthetic route or measured stability. Reproducible provenance and descriptor calculations are in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-11-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json.

per_task.generated_character: Proposals have a median of 25 heavy atoms. Seed 0 concentrates on phenol-substituted pyrazoles with thiocarbonyl/thiourea linkages and unsaturated small carbocycles; seeds 1 and 2 favor alkyl/alkoxy indoles bearing aryl or pyridyl carboxamides. The seed-2 leader at evaluation 298 has 25 heavy atoms, three aromatic rings, an indole NH, ethoxy and methyl groups, a fluoropyridyl group and an N-fluoroamide. Seed 1 reaches an ordinary secondary-amide analogue, whereas the seed-0 leader has four rings, two aromatic, and a hydroxylated cyclobutene substituent. These are recognizable medium-sized heteroaromatic molecules, but the N-fluoroamide and strained/unsaturated ring substitutions make the panel only conditionally plausible as synthetic chemistry. Compared with the Parent, seed 0 shifts from a fused indole-related endpoint into the pyrazole/thiocarbonyl family; seeds 1 and 2 retain the indole/azaaryl-carbonyl neighborhood. Recorded best scores by seed change from 0.442313/0.460926/0.451975 to 0.420196/0.416350/0.438799, with similar molecular scale.
liabilities: The highest observed molecule contains an N-F bond in an amide; a late low-scoring structure combines N-F and O-F bonds with a thiocarbonyl. These are chemically sensitive connectivities, even though the SMILES sanitize.

Cyclobutene/cyclopentadiene substitutions and additional fused closures introduce strain or reactivity concerns; they cannot be treated as routine synthetic analogues solely because they retain the parent functional groups.
missing_features: The upper end does not demonstrate broad alternative ring/linker arrangements that preserve the favorable compact heteroaromatic and polar-group pattern beyond the recurring indole and pyrazole families. A specific absent target motif cannot be inferred from these scores.
Stereodefined forms of the newly substituted nonaromatic rings are not represented; this is a coverage gap, with no score evidence that a particular configuration would help.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole carboxamide scores 0.305105; the compact substituted indole and pyrazole endpoints reach 0.416350 to 0.438799. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 28 and 25, respectively, so retaining a compact heteroaromatic core matters more here than indiscriminate enlargement. The seed-2 evaluation-298 leader scores 0.438799, whereas evaluation 295, which has methoxy and aminomethyl substitutions, scores 0.304901. These are multiple simultaneous differences, not an isolated amine penalty. A Br/F substitution pair in the seed-1 leaders ties at 0.416350, while the elaborate thione/O-fluoro terminal proposal scores 0.091681. Very small proposals such as the cited halogen and hydrocarbon fragments score zero. The observed preference is for a particular compact arrangement of aromatic rings and polar carbonyl/thiocarbonyl groups, with substantial tolerance for chemically unusual substitutions; it does not establish that those unusual bonds cause the gain.

per_task.generated_character: This panel grows large, mostly aromatic assemblies: the proposal median is 69 heavy atoms and nine perceived rings. Seed 0 builds extended azaaryl/aryl carbonyl and ether assemblies; seed 1 repeats aryl and nitrogen/oxygen heteroaromatic carbonyl units with alkoxy, imine, nitrile/cyanate and chloromethyl-ether substituents. The seed-1 evaluation-295 leader has 91 heavy atoms, nine aromatic rings and calculated molecular weight about 1,303.5; evaluation 296 has 113 heavy atoms and 13 aromatic rings. The large repeated products are far outside ordinary small-molecule scale and would require substantial synthetic justification; even the smaller seed-2 series contains unusual reactive functionality. All ordered molecular records and scores match the Parent in all seeds.
liabilities: Very high molecular size, many linked aromatic rings and numerous acceptors create substantial solubility, conformational and synthesis concerns. These are structural concerns, not measured exposure or permeability results.

Chloromethyl ethers, imine/enol-ether segments and the smaller series' N-F/N-Cl/O-Cl bonds require stability and synthetic scrutiny; high scores do not establish that these are isolable, useful compounds.
missing_features: Compact, nonrepeated scaffolds retaining the heteroaromatic/carbonyl/aryl-ether arrangement seen at the upper end are not demonstrated at comparable scores. The missing coverage concerns economical placement of these features, not a shortage of rings or aromatic atoms.

The trajectories do not identify which unseen decoration or reference feature is absent; they show repeated functional-group assemblies rather than evidence for a particular target-specific replacement.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The tiny cited fragments all sit at 0.5. Initial indole and fused ureide-containing molecules already score 0.546402 and 0.548381; elaborated aromatic assemblies reach 0.611413. The low and high score quartiles have median heavy-atom counts of 38 and 85 and median aromatic-ring counts of four and ten. This is an association between the sampled favorable motifs and extensive aromatic elaboration, not evidence that adding arbitrary mass helps. The 91-heavy-atom leader scores 0.611413 and the 113-heavy-atom analogue scores 0.611206, showing that greater size is not monotonically rewarded. Seed 0 reaches 0.609808, seed 1 0.611413 and seed 2 0.597688. Multiple donors/basic sites, brominated aromatic groups and unspecified stereocentres complicate interpretation as a defined medicinal compound; no pKa, permeability or synthetic route is supplied.
Small strained nitrogen rings and NCN aminal connections warrant chemical stability and synthetic review even when the rest of the scaffold uses familiar fragments.
missing_features: Basic nitrogen centres are abundant. What is absent from the submitted representations is explicit protonation and defined stereochemistry for these existing centres and substituted saturated rings; downstream oracle protonation handling is not established by these trajectories.

The favorable compact diaryl/basic-group arrangement has not been broadly reproduced through simpler linkers and routinely closed-shell ring systems. The sulfur branch lacks a demonstrated closed-shell counterpart retaining its high-end arrangement, while the polyamine branch relies on an aminal and many polar/basic sites.

per_task.generated_character: These are mostly medium-sized, densely connected N/O heterocycles: the proposal median is 30 heavy atoms, five rings and two aromatic rings. Duplicating the heterocyclic framework adds size and rings while producing a lower-scoring cited terminal molecule; chemical complexity alone should not be read as meaningful new pharmacophore coverage.

The trajectory does not identify a particular absent reference scaffold.

per_task.generated_character: The proposal median is 27 heavy atoms. Seed 0 reaches compact fluorinated fused ureide-like heterocycles bearing several carbonyls, fluoroalkyl substituents, a fluorinated alkenyl chain and an N-SH substituent. Geometric specification of the unsaturated side chains and defined configurations in the more fused products are missing from the cited SMILES. No trajectory comparison establishes whether assigning those states changes the objective.

A late seed-2 peroxyester-containing molecule scores 0.277703, while its enlarged peroxide-linked relative scores 1.5627949162950568e-19. The gradient clearly does not establish stability or justify peroxide chemistry.

Parse success alone cannot serve as evidence of an ordinary stable molecular product; no objective identity is needed to address this gap.

The cited high-scoring compact indole contains an N-fluoroamide; compact fluorinated ureides carry N-SH; later fused products carry peroxyesters. These are structural flags, not a measured instability count.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically informed ways to vary substituents and heteroatom placement while preserving recognizable functional groups, including stable alternatives to heteroatom-halogen, terminal N-SH and peroxide connections. Apply the same chemical rules and accepted-feedback learning to every objective, without treating an alert as proof that every occurrence is unusable.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support local growth and contraction that retain useful ring/linker context and can remove duplicated substructures. Let already accepted score feedback determine where molecular elaboration matters, while preserving chemically meaningful intermediate sizes; the evidence does not justify one objective-specific size rule or a blanket ban on larger molecules.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve and represent stereochemistry when edits create or modify stereogenic environments, and make alternative configurations available as chemically defined candidates under ordinary identity handling. This adds molecular-state coverage; the supplied scores do not establish which configurations would be favored.

Neutral SMILES do not imply that those compounds stay neutral in solution.

transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support chemically consistent representations of ionizable centres and relevant protonation alternatives using a universal state policy. Preserve the distinction between the submitted representation and any downstream preparation; these trajectories alone neither reveal that preparation nor prove a score benefit from charge enumeration.

possible_failure_causes: The registered score-benefit falsifier is triggered by paired macro delta -0.01754001133127092, below +0.002. Learning noise softens interpolation and changes the posterior draw distribution. On the same Child emissions MSE improves modestly but mean within-batch ranking weakens; this supports a prediction/allocation tradeoff without proving the cause of the downstream score loss.

A plug-in archive scale near 0.001 keeps score-unit uncertainty very small even when standardized noise reaches 0.8. The observed early 157-SD sitagliptin residual directly demonstrates a remaining scale limitation and contributes a large predictive-loss tail; no observations are discarded from the reported calibration.

The selected SD reaches the menu maximum in 116/435 fits. This is evidence that the bounded menu often limits the decision, not evidence that larger noise would improve calibration or search; noise-parameter uncertainty is not integrated.

Latent coverage remains heterogeneous, with decreases in DRD2 seeds 1 and 2 relative to fixed noise on the same emissions. Prospective adaptive selection and a single task-local noise level can leave local mismatch; the audit does not establish a chemical source or stochastic oracle noise.

The molecular assessment finds retained size, electronic-state, functional-group and stereochemical liabilities. Noise modeling changes neither chemical representation nor graph operators, so improved interval statistics cannot establish chemical feasibility or resolve these gaps.

All factorizations succeed at first jitter; numerical recovery and exact-objective tie branches are retained without observed opportunities. Recorded host timers and historical total wall times cannot establish GPU kernel cost or comparative recovery behavior.

A logged selection unconnected to final conditioning does not activate the mechanism. Fits retaining the reference level are valid no-change cases; features and pre-noise kernel entries must remain exactly inherited.

Separate accepted-feedback conditioning, score renormalization and newly selected noise; higher learned noise can prevent the very narrow post-admission uncertainty produced by the reference fit, but before/after uncertainty is not assumed monotone. Terminal scores without another fit and numerical fallbacks are excluded from update opportunities. These probes establish posterior use and update behavior, not prospective accuracy on already admitted scores.
activation_observables.name: Compare pre-feedback predictions with the next fit on the identical emitted molecules, excluding terminal observations with no next suggestion; separate changes in normalization from changes in conditional uncertainty.

Measure one-SD and 1.96-SD latent interval coverage, interval width, standardized residuals, prediction MSE against the same-fit archive-mean baseline and within-batch rank association by task and supplied seed. Also report observed-score predictive variance equal to latent variance plus squared fitted noise in score units, with its coverage, interval width and Gaussian predictive negative log density clearly separated from latent intervals. Compare the learned-noise and fixed-reference-noise predictions on the same actual Child emissions from the same accepted fit data; never assign scores to alternative selected indices or unselected pools. The expected increase is in prospective uncertainty coverage, with interval width and predictive log density showing whether apparent improvement is merely broadening. Marginal-likelihood improvement on training data is not evidence of calibration. Report supplied paired endpoint effects and actual parent-beating outcomes separately; changed downstream trajectories do not isolate an individual uncertainty decision's score.
activation_observables.name: Report chronological prediction MSE against the same-fit archive-mean baseline, within-batch rank association and uncertainty coverage on scored emitted molecules, by task and seed; never infer calibration from posterior arithmetic alone.

A larger selected observation noise should not lower conditional marginal variances against the reference with fixed normalization and the same successful jitter beyond numerical tolerance. Exact binary-fingerprint equivalence and its inability to separate tied feature vectors remain; noise selection does not claim new chemical representation. Count the five bounded trial factorizations separately from final training and pool factorizations, including jitter retries, finite-objective failures and ordinary visible fallbacks. Report unsynchronized host noise-search/fit timings and actual task/runtime and pool completion. The Parent has one final training factorization per successful fit and no noise-search trials. Missing numerical failure opportunities do not demonstrate recovery improvements; historical total runtime differences do not isolate the added fitting cost.

applicability_conditions: The active fingerprint_posterior Layer owns observation-noise modeling. Its accepted-archive and ordered joint-distribution interfaces permit this change while the inherited graph generator, identity handling, scored population and correlated-draw allocation remain frozen.

Noise denotes residual mismatch in the standardized Gaussian surrogate, including information omitted by binary local fingerprints; selecting a larger value does not establish stochasticity of the molecular oracle or identify the chemical source of error.

The selection rule uses only already accepted task-local labels. The same universal five-level menu and tie rule apply to every fit and task, with no task name, historical benchmark score or future emission outcome entering the runtime decision.

Likelihood learning is empirical Bayes with plug-in archive normalization and a bounded discrete noise menu. It neither averages noise-parameter uncertainty nor guarantees calibrated predictions under adaptive selection. Frequent upper-endpoint selection is reported as a menu limitation, without post hoc expansion.

The actual Parent's 254 fixed-data noise-change opportunities establish applicability on recorded accepted archives. They do not provide a new search trajectory or scores for unselected molecules; the Child's changed selected stream must be assessed prospectively.

The supplied count-fingerprint siblings demonstrate a different representation mechanism and unresolved uncertainty coverage. No supplied stable cluster tests this accepted-archive marginal-likelihood noise-selection mechanism. The earlier posterior-sampling cluster concerns introducing allocation by posterior draws, which this experiment inherits rather than revisits.

Larger noise can weaken useful interpolation or enlarge uncertainty on unproductive molecules. Additional bounded factorizations add runtime. Neither uncertainty coverage nor scalar score establishes improved chemical feasibility, size control, stereochemical coverage or robustness outside the supplied panel.
There is no active Round Injection in the authoritative brief.

approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It also retains stable canonical-identity admission and a direct, formula-preserving exchange of aromatic nitrogen positions. Each fresh surplus pool is evaluated by a binary-fingerprint Gaussian process trained on all accepted scores, and correlated posterior draws choose the oracle submissions. Accepted offspring can then enter the breeding population. The posterior currently uses the same small observation-noise level at every fit, even when its prediction errors differ substantially across the molecular neighborhoods encountered.
approach.novelty: Learn that single observation-noise level from the current accepted archive by comparing exact Gaussian marginal likelihoods over a fixed five-level menu. Larger selected noise represents mismatch between fingerprint similarity and accepted scores, reducing how tightly the posterior must interpolate them.
